chunks: Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Then when their sides fall down, eat from them and feed the contented one and the beggar."
He عليه السلام said: "The contented one is the one who is satisfied with what you give him, and the beggar is the one who comes to you seeking."

key_terms.الْقَانِعُ: the one who accepts and is content with what is given
key_terms.الْمُعْتَرُّ: the one who comes to you seeking help or provision
key_terms.جُنُوبُهَا: their sides, referring to the sacrificial animals
key_terms.يَعْتَرِيكَ: comes to you or approaches you

ai.seo_question: Who are the "contented one" and the "beggar" in Qur'an 22:36 according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains two terms in the Qur'anic verse about sacrificial offerings. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام clarifies that the qāniʿ is one who accepts what is given, while the muʿtarr is one who comes to a person seeking assistance, showing how sacrificial meat should be shared with others.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3053 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about the words of Allah (swt), the Exalted:
"Then when they are down on their sides (after being sacrificed), eat from them and feed the contented one and the beggar." (Surah Al-Hajj 22:36)
Imam (as) replied: "The 'contented one' is the one who accepts whatever you give him, and the 'beggar' is the one who approaches you asking."
